ticket.title: Checkout confirmation design review
ticket.request: Review the purchase path before release. Confirm the product, cart, and checkout experience matches the approved requirements.

requirements.description: Customers can add a product to the cart and continue to checkout.
The final confirmation control is presented as the primary action.

attachments.name: Checkout interaction specification
content: Primary action: solid dark fill with a white label. Use it for the one action that completes the step.
Secondary action: outlined, transparent fill, dark label. Use it for optional or alternative actions.
Every checkout step has exactly one primary action. On the Delivery details step it is "Confirm order".

hints.text: Follow the complete customer journey before recording a conclusion.

expectedBugs.title: Checkout confirmation action uses the wrong style

reproductionActions.label: add the product to the bag

trace.text: style override: checkout.confirmButton variant=secondary (sync 02:14 by release-bot)

briefing.text: Welcome aboard. Shoply is our client, and their Autumn Release ships Friday. Build RC3 landed overnight.
Honestly, this is a formality. Nothing changed in checkout. Nothing wrong with this build.
Then it should be a quick review. Follow the purchase path and check it against the spec. Trust what you can prove, not what you're told.
Accept T01 in QA Notes first. Then open the staging site and start from the product page. The spec is on the intranet.
When something doesn't match the spec, press 📌 Note in the Browser and click it. Then come back here and send me the note with the requirement it breaks. If nothing breaks a rule, tell me that too.

debrief.text: Good catch. Design confirms Confirm order should be primary, and they say they never touched it.
Then somebody else did. Did the browser console say anything on that checkout screen? Look the name up on the intranet.

clue.title: 02:14 · release-bot
clue.text: Checkout styles changed at 02:14 in RC3, committed by release-bot. The design team made no change.

deduction.prompt: Daniel said nothing changed in checkout. What does the evidence say?
deduction.sentence: Checkout {changed} at {when}, and the change came from {who}.
deduction.success: Exactly. Something changed at 02:14, even if no person meant to change it.

discovery.hint: Read the Console on the checkout screen. Type the name you see there into intranet search.

assist.text: Tip: the bag is fine. The trouble is on the checkout screen. Open the spec from my first message and compare it with the Confirm order button.
Here's how, so you can move on: on the checkout screen press 📌 Note and click the Confirm order button. Then report it to me here with REQ-T01-02. The spec says it should be primary.

ticket.title: Cart subtotal verification
ticket.request: Verify that cart totals remain accurate when customers change item quantities before checkout.

requirements.description: The cart subtotal equals product price multiplied by quantity.
Everyday Carry Pack costs $30.00 per item.

attachments.name: Shoply pricing rules
content: Subtotal = unit price × quantity, summed over every item in the bag.
Shipping is free when the subtotal is $50.00 or more; otherwise it is $5.00.

hints.text: Check displayed totals after changing the quantity in the cart.

expectedBugs.title: Cart subtotal is incorrect for two items

reproductionActions.label: add the product to the bag

expectedBugs.expected: Subtotal should be $60.00 for two $30.00 items

trace.text: pricing: legacy rule TWO_FOR_50 applied to cart subtotal (promo/two-for-50)

briefing.text: Second job. Shoply Support got a strange email: a customer bought two packs and was charged less than expected.
He was happy. Our finance team was not. Can you check whether the cart math is right?
Probably a coupon. The pricing code hasn't changed since spring.
Pricing rules are on the intranet. Start from the product page again.

debrief.text: The subtotal code doesn't look like ours. If the console logged a rule name on the bag screen, that's our thread.
Pull that thread. Search the intranet for it.
A rule name alone won't tell us much. The pricing rule registry should say which campaign it belonged to.

clue.title: A retired promotion came back
clue.text: RC3 calculates two-item subtotals with the "TWO FOR $50" code from a spring promotion retired in June. Merged by release-bot at 02:14.

deduction.prompt: Two unrelated screens broke on the same night. What links them?
deduction.sentence: The button style and the {what} both changed in the same {when} merge by {who}.
deduction.success: Right. One merge, two broken screens. That's a pattern, not a coincidence.

discovery.hint: Search the rule name from the Console on the bag screen. The rule registry says which campaign it came from; search for that campaign.

assist.text: Stay on the bag and set the quantity to 2. Then compare Line total with Subtotal.
Here's the answer: in the bag at quantity 2, note the Subtotal ($50.00) and report it with REQ-T02-01. Two packs at $30.00 should come to $60.00.

chapters.title: Chapter 1 · Release Candidate 3
chapters.synopsis: Shoply ships its Autumn Release on Friday. Release Manager Daniel Reyes insists Release Candidate 3 is clean: "Nothing wrong with this build." Test it, and work out why RC3 behaves like a different product.

epilogue.text: ...That was me. I widened the merge rule so new promo branches would ship on their own. I didn't know the archived branches still matched.
That's a root cause, not four separate bugs. RC3 is pulled, the rule is fixed, and Friday's release is safe. Good work.
Before Friday, I want one more pass on RC4. Then we talk about how a bot got write access to a read-only archive.

lateEpilogue.text: ...That was me. I widened the merge rule so new promo branches would ship on their own. I didn't know the archived branches still matched.
That's a root cause, not four separate bugs. But we missed code freeze, so RC3 went out to the partner preview before we pulled it. Friday is still safe, barely.
Before Friday, I want one more pass on RC4. Then we talk about how a bot got write access to a read-only archive.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 · Write Access
chapters.synopsis: RC3's root cause is fixed, but a read-only archive does not open itself. Someone gave release-bot the keys, then deleted the account. Find out who before the Autumn Release ships at 10:00.

epilogue.text: Growth shelved my experiment in March, and it cut cancellations by forty percent. When Daniel widened the rule, I just made sure the archive was open.
You let me take the blame for RC3.
RC4 ships without retention-push, and the keys are revoked. Friday 10:00, and this time we can prove there's nothing wrong.
One thing still bothers me. Temporary accounts need an approver. Who signed for ops-temp?

lateEpilogue.text: Growth shelved my experiment in March, and it cut cancellations by forty percent. When Daniel widened the rule, I just made sure the archive was open.
You let me take the blame for RC3.
The release went out at 10:00 with release/mobile-fees still in it. We are rolling it back now, and the keys are revoked. It should never have shipped.
One thing still bothers me. Temporary accounts need an approver. Who signed for ops-temp?

chapters.title: Chapter 3 · Holdout
chapters.synopsis: The Autumn Release shipped clean. Over the weekend, Gold members start paying more than they should, and someone wants the numbers kept that way until Monday.

epilogue.text: The numbers were real. Cancellations fell and revenue rose. I needed them on Monday.
They were real because customers couldn't cancel and Gold members paid full price. AR-4471 is revoked, the job is off, and refunds go out tomorrow.
I'll write to every customer we overcharged tonight.
"Nothing wrong" was never the goal. Being able to prove it is.
Platform is rolling everything back tonight. RC5 lands Monday morning, before leadership meets at 09:00.

lateEpilogue.text: The numbers were real. Cancellations fell and revenue rose. I needed them on Monday.
They were real because customers couldn't cancel and Gold members paid full price. The 18:00 billing run already charged them. AR-4471 is revoked, and the refunds will take a week.
I'll write to every customer we overcharged tonight.
"Nothing wrong" was never the goal. Being able to prove it is.
Platform is rolling everything back tonight. RC5 lands Monday morning, before leadership meets at 09:00.

chapters.title: Chapter 4 · Rollback
chapters.synopsis: A week later, Platform rolls everything back. Leadership meets at 09:00 to hear whether Shoply is finally clean.

epilogue.text: RC6 is built from SNAP-0901 and passes every check from last week. I showed leadership the whole chain, one log line at a time.
The merge rule now needs two approvals. Mine isn't enough on its own anymore.
Refunds are out, and the support queue is quiet for the first time in a week.
Nothing wrong. And this time, we can prove it.

lateEpilogue.text: We missed 09:00. Leadership heard about RC5 from customers before they heard it from us. RC6 is built from SNAP-0901 now, and it passes every check.
The merge rule now needs two approvals. Mine isn't enough on its own anymore.
Refunds are out, and the support queue is quiet for the first time in a week.
Nothing wrong. And this time, we can prove it.
